Paragraph: Summary of Passage: Therefore, curb this destructive impulse right from the beginning by regulating the senses. Slay this formidable enemy that destroys both theoretical knowledge and direct self-realization.
Situation/Problem_Faced: How to proactively interrupt destructive habit cycles before they gain overwhelming momentum.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna instructs Arjuna to conquer desire at the entry point—the senses—right from the very beginning (adau). By regulating sensory habits, one protects wisdom (jnana) and realization (vijnana).
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna receives a practical directive to practice early sensory regulation.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Early Intervention: Stopping negative impulses at the earliest sensory trigger phase
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Sensory Discipline: Setting boundaries on external inputs to guard internal peace
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Preserving Intellectual Clarity: Protecting rational judgment from being corrupted by impulsive urges

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Tasmat tvam indriyany adau niyamya (Therefore, regulating the senses right at the beginning)
Jnanavijnana-nasanam (The destroyer of wisdom and spiritual realization)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: To conquer lust, one must begin by regulating the senses early on. Controlling sensory inputs neutralizes the force that destroys both knowledge of the self (jnana) and practical realization (vijnana).
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Early intervention is key to breaking bad habits. Intercepting a craving at the initial sensory trigger level is far easier than trying to stop a fully escalated emotional or behavioral impulse.
